newsitem.title: SIERRA LEONE: Truce agreed in Sierra Leone, cabinet sworn in.
newsitem.headline: Truce agreed in Sierra Leone, cabinet sworn in.

text.p: Sierra Leone's military ruler and West African field commanders have agreed a truce after bloody weekend clashes between his forces and Nigerian troops south of the capital, officials said on Tuesday.
The two sides agreed the truce during talks in Freetown on Monday that brought together Major Johnny Paul Koroma's military junta and Nigerian, Ghanaian and Guinean commanders, they added.
"Both sides agreed to order all fighting to stop," one military official said.
State radio reported that a new government, announced on July 8, had been sworn in on Monday.
Koroma named a 16-member cabinet team with rebel leader Foday Sankoh, currently under house arrest in Nigeria, as his deputy.

Captain Solomon Musa, deputy leader under a previous military administration, was appointed chief cabinet secretary and mineral resources minister, a key post. It was not clear whether all those nominated had accepted their posts.

Military sources linked the weekend clashes, which killed scores of people according to some reports, to Sierra Leonean irritation at low-flying Nigerian warplanes. Each side say the other fired first.

Nigerian troops, in the country under a pre-coup defence pact, fought soldiers loyal to Koroma and their rebel allies around Jui southeast of Freetown late on Saturday and on Sunday, sending several thousand civilians fleeing from their homes.
Residents of Jui, Benguema and Hastings, towns in the thick of fighting some 15 miles (24 km) from Freetown near Hastings airport, talked of bodies lying in the streets.

The two sides clashed last Wednesday and Thursday at Lungi international airport, across an estuary from the capital as Sierra Leone's People's Army hunted for a clandestine radio station that has broadcast messages from toppled President Ahmad Tejan Kabbah.
Nigerian troops using tanks pushed Sierra Leonean forces out of Lungi town over the weekend.
Nigeria has sent reinforcements as part of efforts to persuade the military junta to restore Kabbah to power after he fell in a coup on May 25.
Impoverished Sierra Leone's West African neighbours have agreed to try dialogue and economic sanctions as methods of persuasion, but have retained the military option.
Kabbah came to power in 1996 after multi-party elections ended four years of military rule.
Revolutionary United Front rebels, who took up arms in 1991, rallied to the coup -- the third in five years.
